thread:
incident-bot: Paging SREs: detected sudden ingress fanout to /v1/embeddings/async that is amplifying requests 25x from a small set of client IPs. Errors rising and cost spike visible on billing dashboard :rotating_light:

maria: seeing 500s on the edge and a lot of long tail latency from worker pools. KV cache miss rate jumped to 82%.

jen: confirmed. A handful of IP blocks show thousands of concurrent connections, same UA string and empty API key header in many. Looks like a scraping proxy farm.

kyle: any customer impact?

maria: some Dedicated customers hitting rate limits, background ingestion jobs slowed. Hosted customers reporting higher tail latency on embeddings. No full outage yet.

ryan: immediate mitigation options: 1) apply WAF rule to challenge/block the offending UA pattern 2) soft-quota slice for embeddings per-API-key 3) disable async-batch ingestion endpoint behind a feature flag.

jen: +1 to WAF and feature-flag. We should prefer rate-slicing to avoid breaking legit traffic. Suggest a geo fence for the top offending ASNs too.

maria: putting proposed edge rule: 
```
edge-waf rule: if header[User-Agent] matches /python-requests\/2\./i AND header[Authorization] is missing then block with 403
rate-limit: per-ip 10r/s burst 20
```

deploy-bot: rollout queued: edge-waf/v2 -> canary -> 5% -> 2026-03-17T15:28Z

kyle: can we also do per-customer soft quotas? We can slice embedding tokens for accounts exceeding baseline by 3x and return Retry-After 60. That will protect Dedicated capacity.

maria: implementing soft-slice policy now. Patch applied to routing layer: `routing.slice_threshold=3x` and `response.header.Retry-After=60` for exceeded keys.

jen: I'm running a quick smoke: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/async -d '{"input":"test"}' -> 200 OK during canary.

ryan: WAF canary in 2 mins, will monitor 5m windows. Metrics to watch: 5xx rate, kvcache hitrate, tokens/sec, cost delta.

incident-bot: oncall note: handoff to night shift in 30m if still active. Current severity: P2 (high traffic + customer perf).

maria: initial WAF canary blocked ~72% of offending IPs and dropped request rate by 18%. KV cache miss down to 57%. Good signal.

jen: rolling WAF to 50% now, hold on disabling async-batch for all customers.

kyle: customer comms draft: "We observed increased abusive traffic affecting embeddings latency for a subset of customers. We've applied mitigation and may throttle excessive concurrent requests. If you see problems, contact support." QA?

ryan: fine to send once WAF at 100%. Ops to include per-customer impact list.

maria: WAF at 100%. Token burn dropped 37%. Dedicated pools stable. No further 500 spikes.

jen: marking mitigations: WAF UA+no-auth rule, per-key soft-slice with Retry-After, geo/ASN blocks added. Leaving async-batch enabled but with stricter concurrency.

incident-bot: action items assigned: maria -> confirm long-term ASN blocks and update firewall list; kyle -> implement automatic quota-slice rule in policy engine; jen -> prepare post-incident notes + cost impact; ryan -> prepare handoff summary for night oncall.

maria: starting follow-up runbook updates now.

kyle: ETA for quota engine change: 2 hours. Will try to get a fast patch in 45m.

jen: will notify affected customers in the next hour after correlating impacted accounts.

ryan: handing off to night oncall @jen in 30m. If anything spikes, escalate to SRE pager. :white_check_mark:
